She does offer plenty of extra credit and her class was fairly easy because of how she made it and the resources she provided. As for the R assignments my TA would do the whole thing in discussion and we would just copy it lol but yeah very easy if you just put a little effort but you're better off teaching yourself with her resources.

As someone who did pretty poorly in this class, I think some of the reviews (especially ones from the middle of the semester) are slightly exaggerating because emotions were high and so people were reactionary. That being said, I don't think she's a particularly good professor (she has flaws) but she's not like the literal devil The Bad: - the course was kind of poorly organized, and I think that her disorganization and lack of transparency around it is what caused a LOT of the problems. The extra credit system is a pretty strong example of this - there were a variety of things you could get credit for but it wasn't always clear how much credit you were getting/whether you were getting it/how it would actually impact your grade. She also had a really confusing policy about dropped quizzes (she automatically dropped one but if you did poorly on quiz1 but well on quiz2 your quiz2 grade would replace your quiz1 grade and wouldn't count as the dropped quiz, but she also mentioned this being based on individual student evaluation?) which she then fixed by just dropping 2 quizzes for everyone and saying she intended to all along and just lied to motivate us. I don't know if she's lying about that but it's kind of mean to just lie about a course policy for the sake of "motivation" - she gave out extra credit for Piazza but didn't really define what counted as a contribution worthy of getting points, so the STAT400 piazza was kind of a pain in the ass since everyone was just responding to things for the sake of getting points, even if they didn't know what was going on or have a good answer (sometimes students answered posts about logistics that instructors should have answered, sometimes you would get 4 people in the followups saying the same thing, or editing the student answer for the sake of getting more contributions, it was all very annoying) - the rubrics for this class were bad, it was really hard to know what I actually lost points on (the graders overuse the point adjustment feature, and the rubrics themselves aren't the most clear) - sometimes the answer keys had errors: apparently this was on purpose for the sake of the extra credit system but I think that's a bad choice. If someone catches the mistake and gets extra credit that's cool for them, but I imagine plenty of people just got more confused because they were looking at an answer key that was wrong, and they probably didn't learn the content correctly because they assumed the answer key was right - she didn't let us see our final (like it wasn't on Gradescope) after it was graded which was annoying because I would have liked to know what I did wrong - lecture wasn't super engaging (I will also admit fault here, I slept through some of them, they were at 9:30am in the armory) and I think she would probably be better at a different time (that wasn't so early), I think part of the issue is that she went pretty slowly through the set theory and combinatorics stuff, which made the first lectures really boring for anyone who kind of knew it, and also meant that when she went through the harder stuff, there was less time for it than there ideally would have been - the canvas was organized poorly, it's just kind of hard to find things in the files there, which is annoying The Good: - she's not terrible at explaining things, and she's pretty patient. Sometimes this is to her detriment (she entertained way too many questions from people who probably should have just gone to office hours, it kind of disrupted the flow of lecture) but it was nice in lecture. She also lets people do the questions on the board which is fun! I like that - her TAs were all really nice! I never learned any of their names except my TA's, but my TA was really nice, and when I asked for clarification from the other TAs during the exams, they were all very nice - quizzes weren't too bad, they were usually pretty similar to the discussion practice sheets. The discussion practice sheets were also pretty helpful. I didn't do amazing on the quizzes but that's kind of a skill issue on my part - She does post notes, which is nice - The homeworks weren't easy but they weren't unreasonable imo, I could have done better on them if I didn't procrastinate so much, she does also drop some I believe tl;dr - I don't think I would recommend her, and I don't think I would take a class with her again, but I also think a lot of these reviews make her seem way worse than she is. You don't need to like avoid her at all costs or anything. I think a lot of people expected this class to be easy because she made it super easy for the previous semester, and then people got upset when it was harder. I think this class was probably more challenging than it needed to be (Exam2 was bad for everyone) but I think she'll probably improve in the coming semesters

Truly a 4 star professor but his reviews are a bit crazy, so I want to raise his rating a bit higher. Like others have said, do the homework, review the practice exams, and you should be fine with this class. Coding projects are a bit annoying but they are not hard. Would recommend.

Hard class but the subject is fun. Midterms were brutal. They were worth 20% of your grade, and out of 20 points. So each point you lose is one point off your final grade. Final was 40%. Substantial curve at the end so it was okay. He covers stuff most STAT410 Professors don't: multivariate normal and random vectors, some stuff on Monte Carlo Simulation, and has a very theoretical focus (or so he says). He uses random walks for most of his examples. Exams are designed to test your understanding and are not plug and chug. No cheat sheet. Overall if you think you're smart, take him. He'll give you a better class than most people teaching STAT410.

Teaching: He mixes his lectures with both SAS programming and statistics and overall does a good job teaching the material. He is knowledgeable in the content topics and always encourages students to ask questions. He often go on tangents or talk about his research, but he always relate it to statistics. Personality: Professor Kedem is pretty funny and approachable. Grading: Grading is not a big deal and accepts late homework/projects(even those that are weeks late). He doesn't treat you like kindergartens. If for example, you got a C on your midterm, and you received an A on your final. He'll give you an A.

Vadim was a pretty good professor. His lectures were easy to follow, exams were fair, and course load was never overbearing, which is all I can ask from a Gen-ed. Attendance was *technically* not mandatory, but about 60-70% of lectures had in-class assignments to be done in small groups. They were always easy, and I'm pretty sure everyone that attended class always got a perfect score, but I didn't love that aspect. He also would not say if there would or would not be an assignment beforehand, though I assume that is because he knew many people would not attend if they knew there were no assignment. Exams had review sessions with the TA, and the recording and slideshow were posted on ELMS, which made studying pretty quick and straightforward. You were also allowed 2 sheets of notes, front and back, for each midterm, as well as 4 for the final. Lowest exam was dropped, which was really nice. Much of the class didn't even need to take the final. Lastly, this was one of Vadim's first semesters teaching, and he really pushed for honest feedback from us, which I think highlights his passion as well as him wanting to improve his class for future years. If I were to take this class again, I'd choose Vadim's class again.

Legit FREAKING AMAZING!!!! She is the best professor I have ever had at UMD. Her class is very easy to follow, and her slides have EVERYTHING you need to know for the tests. She is pretty young, so shes pretty funny and relatable. If you try, and study in this class, you will do well. Also she really does try to learn a ton of peoples names in a huge lecture hall, which is rare. Please take her. I am so glad I did. (she had no reviews when I signed up haha)

I never met Professor Mohan, but I've heard she is extremely scary even from my TA so it's ok. The pre-labs are pretty easy however you have to pay attention to small details, luckily you have two attempts on each one. There were no exams but was a poster project which was really easy as long as you have a good group. You kind of work out your lab groups on the first day so pick wisely. Having a good group is really beneficial not just for assignments, but for efficiency in class. Volunteer to go first for as much as you can because usually, you will get out earlier than other groups. READ EVERYTHING it is straightforward but they will take points off for the littlest of things. The major things in this class are completing the pre-lab quiz, lab manual, poster project, 1 lab report, and the lab practical. The lab practical is super easy. I would highly recommend going to office hours before the lab practical because the TAs literally walk you through it. They also post an example of the exam on canvas which makes it easy to see what you need to know. Overall this lab is easy but annoying.

Dr. Goytia was an incredible professor who showed her passion and interest for the material that she taught. She was very resourceful when you needed a question answered and responded timely to emails. Her exams were very fair and if you pay attention in class then you should be able to understand the content pretty well. She also provides extra credit throughout her exams plus another extra credit paper after the exam to bring your grade up. Make sure to stay on top of things in this class since all the units build on each other. Dr. Goytia was also very approachable for any questions or clarification you may need

Dr. Fletcher is a great person, very friendly and approachable. This class is a LOT of content, you were expected to know specific lineages of random animals and random facts. This class built on previous bio classes so you needed to have background knowledge because he doesn't explain basics like cellular respiration. I actually had no clue how to study for this class as it is purely memorization although he does let you have a cheat sheet (1-sided). I recommend the GSS worksheets, they were like recaps. The GAE (group activities) and homework were graded on completion so that did help with my grade a bit. The recorded lectures were really helpful because the lectures were packed with content so if you missed something, you can always look back on it. He drops one exam score and one assignment from each category. I thought the 2nd unit was the toughest because it was very very specific, you either know it or you don't. The final wasn't too hard, it was about 50% new content and 50% old content. Overall this is probably the most boring biology class I've taken but Dr. Fletcher made it bearable.

One of the best professors I have ever taken! He is genuinely interested in teaching the content and is always willing to help if you attend office hours. There are a lot of assignments for the class, and they are single-attempt, but they are fairly easy if you understand the concepts. I think these assignments definitely helped me stay on top of the material since I needed to understand the content before taking the quizzes. The assignments are essentially free points that help boost your grade. The exam content is very similar to the practice exams. My advice would be to complete a few practice exams and then go over the answers to past practice problems—since he has exams dating back to 2009—to ensure you're not missing any important material. He also shares past final exams, which I haven't seen any other professor do. He hosts weekly review sessions where he goes over previous exams, and during exam week, he holds a Zoom review session that is not recorded (though everything else is).

Kendall was a great TA, super chill and helpful in lab. Super receptive about fixing grades, we had a discussion about why I answered a test question the way I did and once I explained my reasoning she fixed my grade immediatley. Genuinely wants everyone to get an A in the class. Make sure you clean up your lab bench before you leave or you might get points off. Showed us lots of pics of her cute dog :)

Consistently late to class. He once moved an exam two days before it was scheduled, then emailed everyone that he couldn't make it the day of the exam. Unbelievably difficult to pay attention to, this man needs to take INAG110

I'm sure it's been repeated enough, but to do well in Dr. Payne's class, you need to know everything on his slides. Practice tests are a good depiction of what you should expect on the tests. I thought he was a great teacher and his lectures were interesting.

He was an okay professor, but his lectures were so boring I slept most of the time.... He posts past exams and reuses some questions and/or makes new questions off of old ones, so make sure to go through those. But I feel like I did not learn a single thing this semester, it was truly a waste of my time and energy. I also was so close to an A- (2% off) so that was disappointing. Don't recommend taking him if you want to take this class.

Taking this over the summer probably wasn't the best idea. I grasped the pace of the course while taking it. Orgo requires a lot of memorization, which does not couple well with a short amount of time. Also, a solid foundation of it is key to succeeding in Orgo 2. Professor Koppel is not as bad as I thought. She cares and does her best. However, it's just difficult to sit through 10 hours of lecture consecutively in a week, alongside the lab. Not recommended over the summer!
I was supposed to receive a 94% but my grade was curved down 6% to a B+. This pulls down my GPA by several points. If you can avoid it, do not take a class with Dr. Guest.

I'd highly recommend avoiding this professor. He mumbles a lot and talks very quietly so he's not very easy to understand. He's very bad at teaching and his lectures are honestly a waste of time. He glosses over hard-to-understand topics such as quantum mechanics and organic chemistry. He requires you to buy the $80 textbook only for him to not use it a single time the entire semester. The homeworks are nothing like the exams and just weekly busywork. He's the only professor of CHEM135 that doesn't make his exams open notes. Overall, his class was a waste of time and money. Do not take him.

Good teacher, very nice -> first time teaching the class collectively but is genuine and cares for his students to succeed. Not sure about curves right now but the way he's teaching it makes a lot more sense (coming from a person retaking Chem 231 -> f*ck Dixon). He tends to go a little fast and past lecture time but it's not the end of the world. You also get plenty of resources.

i have never seen koppel or contacted her the whole time, its mainly the TAs doing everything. for a 1 credit class, it is a bunch of work. every week you have to do a pre lab write up & worksheet(s) for the current week and then the post lab questions & worksheet(s) for the previous weeks. the PLQs are so hard and long, sometimes the worksheets are confusing as well but the pre lab write ups are fine. i learned this later on in the semester (wish i started in the beginning), but you HAVE to go to the TAs office hours to make your life easier. especially find a TA who will just give you the answers bc some are stuck up and will only help if you attempt the question. there was a curve, i dont think any other reviews really mentioned this but my 78 got rounded to a B.

Don’t be fooled by all the overly positive comments, everyone I know who took Dixon was miserable. Honestly feels like she’s writing the good reviews herself. The only way to do well in this class was to go to office hours constantly, because lecture alone was not enough. I get that orgo is supposed to be hard and time consuming, but this class took it to another level. The amount of outside effort required just to keep your head above water was exhausting. Not a good experience overall.

Overall, I think that Kahn is nice, pretty approachable, and obviously cares about how his students feel and the feedback they have to offer. I would think that the class is more difficult compared to a typical general chemistry 2 class, but as long as you do his old exams and mostly pay attention in lecture, you should be fine. You can tell he has a passion for teaching, but sometimes he can go on tangents or go into too much detail in lecture, which can be confusing. He does hold 2 hour or more review sessions outside of class time before each exam though, which most professors don't do. If I had to make the choice of which chem professor to take again, Kahn would be my choice.

Epic fail class. 3 exams + final for a 2 credit class. There is a ridiculous amount of work for this class as well. Lab reports aren't short and the grading is VERY VERY inconsistent. I've compared my lab reports with others and some people will get points deducted and others won't for the same answer. It was difficult to study for exams. It was strongly based on application of the material. There was 1000 points total. CHEM271, the corresponding lecture, had only 500 points total and the work load was very small.
if you have him, just know that every one-star review you see here is true and even worse.

Monotonous lecturer but still gets the point across. His exam averages are extremely low, which shouldn't be a problem if every other 132 professor has exam averages that low. But that isn't the case; for the first two exams of the Spring 2025 semester, we had averages in the mid to low 60s. The third exam had an average in the mid 70s. This wouldn't be a problem if 132 were a weed-out class, but it seems like only Pedram treats it like one. At the end of the day, he isn't a terrible professor but his exams are unnecessarily hard.

This class was an absolute hell scape. Final grades just got posted this morning, Christmas Eve, when the final was on December 12th. I guess he was grading his final project 6 grades as well - which had a due date of December 20th???? My final grade was a 76, which between about 3 extra credit points (which he said applied post curve?) got me to a B. I learned way more watching YouTube videos and googling the content on the lecture slides than I did going to this mans lectures. I still went to lectures, unlike 50% of the class, because his Panopto recordings are basically useless otherwise. This man LOVES his chalkboard - and none of it gets picked up by Panopto. It gets better. No one in the back 60% of the class can read the chalkboard either. His handwriting kinda sucks, but its also just small? As a back of the class sitter, I had to go to the front because I couldn't read not only the chalkboard, but also the code on the screen. He also likes to mumble. Also, god forbid you have a yapper in the class... dude has no self control and will have an entire conversation with one student about the most niche topic thats not even remotely related to the lecture. As for discussions, no one goes (unless you have a really good TA, which most don't). They teach you things in discussions at the beginning of the year that they don't teach in lecture. That's where we learned gdb commands and stuff about valgrind and splint. You're also supposed to go over memory maps in discussion, but my TA was running behind so we never got to it, and lo and behold I did bad on the memory map questions :'(. Either way, these things show up on exams, and aren't taught in lecture; but, they are all recorded, so you can watch yours *or* your favorite TA's recordings. Honestly, I didn't think the projects were awful. That was actually where I did best in the class. The worst thing about them is the like week and a half deadline... combined with my awful schedule I was often pulling an all-nighter a day or two before it was due. The project I did worst on was when I was like deadly sick for a week and then just didn't finish it well. And then the next project relied on it lol. I usually lost a few points on them, but not a ton. This is 35% of your grade so it's important to focus on these. The exams are the real reason everyone hates this man. 50% of your grade is exams (actually lower than most coding classes from what I've seen, but still a lot). He will post "practices" like 3 days before exams and quizzes, saying they are supposed to help you. Sometimes the content on them is literally not on the exam/quiz AT ALL??? He likes to do this to waste your time :). What you actually need to be doing is studying the most obscure edge case you've never been taught, a bunch of random linux and gdb commands you were never taught, and just like 3 or 4 pretty hard coding questions. All that studying only for class averages of 67, 66, and 65 for the midterms and final, respectively. Me personally, I genuinely didn't have enough time to study well, so I did like 5-10% worse than average on the midterms, and then did almost 10% better on the final. For the quizzes, we had means of 62 and 66! The only thing he does to help boost your grade is the coding exercises and lab work. There were 10 lab assignments and 4 exercises, with a fifth exercise for 2% extra credit. These are generally easy and are about 15% of your grade. However, if you miss the announcement that they get posted, you might lose points for turning in late/not at all. tl:dr, if you are a normal student, the grades will be super low, and you will likely be super stressed. While Yoon is genuinely a nice person, he is a very mean professor. You will be stressed for both exams and projects. Make sure you teach yourself the content, and try your best not to fall behind. If you didn't read the grade data posted above - 17% of people fail this class, and like 8% withdraw. If all the registration spots close for every other professor like they did for me, I am very sorry, and good luck.

do not take him. please save yourself. genuinely my biggest college regret is taking fawzi over teli. fawzi is such a harsh grader you can study so long and understand the concepts but your grades just won’t reflect that bc he seems to enjoy showing off his ego rather than figure out how to best help his students do better. don’t take him, and save yourself. please

Terrible teacher plain and simple. He's lazy, slow, and unorganized. His homeworks are quite literally, look up shit and copy and paste the AI overview. I learned nothing from this course. Max is also quite an insufferable teacher, he pretends that his exams are difficult because they're are application based but in reality they're difficult because we've never learned how to apply anything. A couple times he'll introduce things and say we don't need to know it but you actually do. He'll introduce a million different concepts, barely scratch the surface of each topic, then expect you to know how to apply the concept like you were part of a large corporation and implementing a real-world model. Expect nothing to be graded until a month after the late deadline and tons of inconsistencies in the rubric. An answer on our first exam was incorrect (he admitting it was incorrect) and now at the end of the semester it still has not been fixed and some people still have unprocessed regrade requests. By far the worst professor I've had so far, I was maybe interested in half of one lecture. Some of the 5 star reviews are probably Max himself.

He's a great public speaker I think the first half of the semester he was getting back into teacher but after that he was getting better at lecturing. He does clicker quizzes which to be honest only people who don't want to show up to lecture complain about it's a free 4% of your entire grade he essentially gives people answers to it most of the time and there not hard questions. As for projects, exams, and quizzes he co taught with Cliff so most of the projects and exams were made by Cliff and his TAs from my understanding. Between Cliff or him Anwar is the better 330 professor provides great slides to study off and is more entertaining/ easier to follow.

Took this class in the summer. Layout was 1 exam every two weeks for a total of 3. I believe he mentioned he cut some small part of the normal material out to make sure we had enough time to cover everything. Justin was always very understanding about everything and very receptive on Piazza, I definitely recommend taking this class over the summer if you get the opportunity.

Awful, awful professor. Lectures are incredibly high level with absolutely no application involved. Grading scripts make countless errors, which he promises to resolve, but WILL NOT ALWAYS if you are unlucky. Incredibly disorganized course webpage.

Honestly, one of the most unorganized classes I've ever taken. Avoid this professor at all costs. The first project took nearly 2 months to get back to us, and over half of the students got zeroes due to shoddy testing code. Every assignment we've had so far has had to be regraded. This morning, the day AFTER the drop deadline, he announces the next midterm and final exam will be in class rather than take-home. Completely unprofessional.

I took Meesh's class in 2003, and TA'd for 420 twice. You can blame me for the XML input the projects still use today. Meesh was the best 400 level professor I had. I learned more in her class than any other at UMD.

I think the professor taught as best as he could, but the class structure just wasn't good at all. The TAs never responded on Piazza so he was basically the only one who ever answered questions, grades took forever to get back, lectures weren't recorded for unexplained reasons, and the slides were taken from UC Berkeley and never updated. Pratap has potential to be a great professor, but if he's gonna teach this class in the future he should just make his own slides, and he should push the TAs to at least answer student questions.

I had an amazing experience in CMSC424 with Prof Keleher. I think many of the 1-2 star reviews judge Keleher a little too negatively. I liked this class and the way Keleher taught it. Pros: 1) Keleher actively responds to Piazza posts and answers student questions in office hours and is very understanding if you communicate with him proactively 2) Weekly lecture quizzes had questions and solutions that helped prepare for the exams and final 3) Assignments were well-explained and not too difficult to implement 4) He posted practice exams with problems, detailed answer keys, and topic lists to prepare 5) He answered questions in lecture and recommends good resources and sections in the textbook 6) TAs are responsive and had both online/in-person OH and responded to my Piazza questions quickly and private posts 7) Cutoffs for the overall grades were pretty generous 8) Well organized, good logistics and regular announcements on Piazza 9) Topics covered in class are very applicable to real-life database engineering Cons: 1) Doesn’t record lectures which I found a little challenging at times as hearing his personal commentary would have helped supplement my understanding of the material Other than that, this was an excellent course that I learned a lot from and I would definitely recommend taking it with Keleher.

Reeks of tenure. TAs did literally everything for this course. Lectures had nothing noteworthy in them, and we were not able to practice these concepts. Projects had very odd grading schemes and had no input from the instructor. Midterm exam (conceptual and explanatory) was extremely different from the one given as practice (computational and short). The only reason students did well was because he did not give installation instructions for a MATLAB package for M1 Macbooks, so after 2 weeks of no information we've been told our final project (20% of the final grade) has been made optional. Very uninteresting course and experience.

(Disclaimer: had him during fall 2020 virtual semester) I found the course a lot easier than 351. The homeworks were a bit challenging but I found that the TAs, at least during this semester, graded very generously (the rubrics are not like 351 where it’s basically 0%, 50%, or 100% per question). The tests were kind of hard to do under a time crunch but they were generally easier than the homeworks and again had generous rubrics. Childs is a nice professor and responsive to the students - he extended the deadline on one of our homeworks. If you’re interested in 451 I recommend taking it with him.

Dr. Washington is an amazing professor! He teaches concepts very clearly, is a super nice guy. He's very understanding about workload and will give you any extensions you need. Exams are very fair, and I had fun putting in what work I could to learn the material (I was also taking cmsc414 and cmsc320 that semester). Definitely take a class with him before you graduate!

not sure why there's the hate in the some of these reviews... professor was very clear that the course was going to be asynchronous from the beginning. and whenever i did go to lecture he was really helpful and nice. i didn't have to waste time going to lectures and labs for stuff i already knew or could easily google which saved me so much time. there were other in-person sections for 326 too, feel like some people would've just had a better experience there. honestly this was one of the best classes i've taken, but to each their own ig

Avoid taking this class if you don't want to teach yourself calculus. The only reason I'm not giving a one-star review is because I think she's a nice lady at heart and she's kind of funny sometimes, but she's a terrible teacher. Her tests are overly difficult as well and the review that she does in class provides minimal help in preparing for the exam. I've tried studying different ways for each exam and I always pick the hardest problems I can find in the textbook and do all the recommended problems in the syllabus, and she always finds a way to pick questions that are both unheard of and harder than the practice problems. As someone that didn't take calculus in high school, as a first-time learning experience this is probably one of the worst ones I could've had.

Yea there's basically nothing bad to say. Every review has basically already covered it. He's incredibly nice and understanding. And you'll walk out of the class learning something while having a good time. If you have the option to take him, do it!

intro: overall i think i liked the class and coursework? if you want to know why 3 stars, see the cons section below the class itself is not very hard and she makes the class pretty easy in multiple ways pros: - quizzes are given about weekly/biweekly depending on exams/break, and you can work in groups of 2-3 within your discussion section (so make sure you're in the same discussion as your friend if you care) - 2 practice exams per midterm given before, which are formatted very similar to the actual midterm. also a lot of resources for finals like practice/past exams - she does a LOT of review sessions, for midterms and a couple for finals (which look generally useful if you're lost on a topic), mostly over zoom/recorded but sometimes in person; i never went to these but she gave useful info there - she posts her edited/unedited notes on the ELMS files page so you can follow along and/or catch up, but very rarely the notes might not make any sense alone (without her explanations in lecture) if you don't already understand the foundation/previous content that its building on - always posts reminders/announcements about review sessions/quizzes/projects and generally seems pretty responsive/available to help - midterms/finals were, for me, easier than the practice versions or the review session problems - couple of points of extra credit on exams - 2 quizzes dropped? - she seems very kind and helpful - discussions are mainly extra practice problems for content you're on, and i didn't attend after 2/3 of semesters when things got busy and I still did well overall (besides required for quizzes) neutral: - no assigned homework/graded homework if you want that for a grade boost, however she does assign problems from the textbook (which she provides, online) for you if you want extra practice. i didn't need any of it to do well on exams/quizzes - the way that the notes are written during lecture can sometimes be messy. there's a general format of definition/theorem -> examples but this can change from time to time - 4 matlab projects, i found the content/questions asked here somewhat more confusing than in-class, and sometimes its a little unclear of what the question exactly is asking for/how you can get to the answer, but overall not a bad part of the course - she has a decently heavy accent which if that's hard for you to listen to/understand, it could be a possible issue -- additionally, shes not fluent in english like a native speaker, which is fine, but you just have to be more careful when listening to make sure you understood correctly - sometimes makes a mistake during lecture which slows down the class which is fine overall cons: - here's my MAIN issue with the class: going to lecture was such a terrible experience (for me) - besides the accent (for me personally), she had very odd/fluctuating pacing throughout each lecture; she would either be really slow with question/problem making it boring, or be really fast with a question and you can't write any notes down - on top of pacing, sometimes she'll be late and then hold the lecture for like 2-3 minutes after class and only slightly mention "this will be really important: ..." after doing miscellaneous work the entire lecture - she repeats herself like, a lot. like 3-5+ times at certain points in lectures. then she might also move on quickly and you won't know if shes still on the same example #1 or suddenly on example #10 - she always expects class engagement in the lecture (or even in review sessions). she'll either like have the answer up on the screen and then ask us for the answer (literally waiting for someone to say something), or she'll just repeat a question like 4 times asking what the answer is (even if its painfully obvious/basic arithmetic) - she switches between an ipad screen/her paper notes at times, slowing down class but also why can't we just stick to the screen format which is easier to read/follow along - explanations for concepts are IFFY at BEST, and generally just not helpful at all. she'll switch through a various bunch of concepts quickly and sometimes you'll fall behind on what's going on in class (or she'll move backwards in content while you're still writing down an example) --> THIS was honestly one of my bigger issues; her explanations are just not good -- additionally, I just didn't find her explanations useful for new concepts and I was often rather confused after a lecture on what she meant. (but it does seem like she knows what shes talking about) - she has a lot of expectations of what terms you understand/know and will quickly mention some new word/vocab in class but not actually explain what it means so its like a double layer of confusion - overall, i just had such an entirely bad experience with attending her lectures i pretty much dreaded the days I this class's lecture - lectures themselves are not recorded if you care conclusion/tldr: - class was on the easier side and shes very helpful, kind, and provides many resources to succeed but the lectures were approaching unbearable (for me).

I would not recommend taking Professor Zhao. In his lectures, he simply prints pages from the textbook and works through the derivatives of the equations on the chalkboard. The examples he provides are the same ones found in the textbook, and he solves them extremely quickly. As a result, unless you had reviewed the material before class, it was difficult to fully comprehend the information. When introducing new topics, he rushes through them. Before THANKSGIVING, we had already finished all of the course material. During the following two weeks, each class consisted of reviewing two textbook chapters within 50 minutes. For one of the hardest topics, Vector Fields, we learned all of the theorems in less than two weeks. The only saving grace of the class was my TA, who reviewed the material thoroughly and was far more helpful than the professor. Even the TA expressed confusion about why the professor rushed through the entire textbook. The grading breakdown was 10% quizzes, 25% midterm, 25% midterm, and 40% final. The averages were midterm 1, 74%, midterm 2, 73%, and final, 70%. The class is basically just self-review the whole time, and going to the lecture is a waste of time.
Definitely take this class with her. She goes over multiple examples in class, responds to emails in a timely manner and her way of teaching is very easy to follow.

I'm not a fan of Truman. Homework assignments took hours and weren't similar to any of the problems we covered in class. The averages for the exams were all around 50%. I would go for a different professor when taking 310.

Had him for MATH461 and decided to take MATH401 with him as well. The class was a good experience, and Allan was always quick to reply to my countless emails asking for clarification regarding the content. The exams were very fair. The work load isn't light per se, but it helped me understand the content.

Dr. Cohen is not that bad, but for me, 403 was a challenging course. The exams were hard because you had to recall a lot of the theorems from chapters that might not have been covered recently. Going to the math dept. tutor, Dr. Bhatia, helped a lot. If you do take this class, make sure you are comfortable with proofs and algebraic concepts in general.

Very nice guy and a pretty good professor. His tests are very reasonable and he gives you practice tests too. He is very approachable during office hours. He assigns homework bi-weekly. He collects 2 or 3 problems and then quizzes you on another 2. However, in class before the quiz, you can ask him ANY homework problem and he will do it. There's usually enough time to do all of them, so you're set for the quiz. He'll also do problems in office hours. With a little effort, you can get a 100% in homework and quizzes.

Great professor who you can tell really knows and enjoys the content he's teaching and wants you to understand it too. Follows the textbook very closely - but unlike some other professors, manages to present the material in a way that adds onto the textbook and truly makes class worth attending. He's also generally really nice, exams are fair, and homework load is manageable. I'd highly recommend him.

He is really good at teaching, and thoroughly enjoys it. Even in an upper level class, no question was too basic, and the lectures were given at a reasonable pace with full explanation. In other words, all assumptions and previous assertions or connections to previous parts of the problem were made clear at each step. Homework was also very reasonable but helpful, and he strikes a nice balance between proofs and applications (i.e. USING the concepts). Lectures were very helpful, and focused on a lot of examples of methods used to prove and solve things. He is also very helpful (and always present) at office hours. I might say that the class is a little less rigorous than I remember 410 and being and than other 411 classes I've heard about, but he does a healthy amount of relating the material to topo and linear. I would definitely say that even a very introductory view of set theory/topo is extremely useful the first unit in his class.

Dr. Hassam is awesome! He is so friendly and funny – he tries to make lecture entertaining. The examples he gives in class are not nearly as hard as the ones on the exams, but if you go to discussion and understand MasteringPhysics problems, you will be very well prepared for exams. I had Jack for my TA and he was very helpful. Lab is hard, but I still managed to get an 89% for my total lab grade. There are also occasional quizzes in discussion, which count for 5% of your grade, about a dozen MasteringPhysics homeworks (15%), two midterms (15% each), the final (30%), and lab counts for 20%. Hassam gives a very generous curve. The midterms consists of about 4 multiple choice/ true or false questions and about 4 problems. I did well in lab and on homework, but I failed most of the exams and still received a B in the course. He assigns grades relatively, meaning you are graded according to how everyone else in the class performs. Dr. Hassam doesn’t like to fail anyone if he can help it. If you study hard, do all of the homeworks, and attend every discussion you will do well in this class.

Class structure: Incredibly disorganized. Due dates constantly changing. One assignment is due, then the date is shifted, then it is no longer due. You already did it? Too bad. Am I in a physics class or a Kafkaesque fever dream? Teaching style: Goes through pre-written PowerPoint slides that make no sense even when he tries to explain things. He is not a good communicator so he dislikes teaching, which makes class a giant waste of time. Feedback style: Shockingly nasty. Says things like "it's not my job to teach you xyz..." "I guess you weren't paying attention during class..." "Any lack of success is your own doing." Office hours: One of my classmates said he showed up to office hours and Severson said he was busy "come again next week". Excuse me? Office hours is when you make yourself available to your students. Lab: 3 hours of blind confusion where you learn nothing about physics. It is just about decoding the instructions and then messing around on excel. They aren't even his labs but he doesn't care enough to change them. Difficulty: It was an easy class if you ignore him and just learn from online resources. Overall: He is an unfortunate reminder that not all teachers care about their students. He would just prefer to rant, ramble, and blame his students rather than take responsibility for the quality of his own course.

Hailu is a decent professor if you can look past his boring lectures. The actual content is very useful, and he answers students' questions well. Exams are fair, and the final, while difficult, was also fair. Does plenty of practice problems like the exams in lecture, so please actually go to them. Like other reviews say, he doesn't post much practice material; please practice from the textbook and you will be fine. Tip: if you sit toward the front near him, you will be less likely to fall asleep.

The only truly great physics professor at UMD in my (limited) experience. His exams aren't necessarily easy, but they're direct and worded well so that if you understand the proper concepts you will succeed. Helpful guy overall with a keen sense of humor and the passion to make otherwise lackluster content seem interesting enough to learn. Only slight on him is that he doesn't update canvas nearly as much as he should, but otherwise is the best bet by far if you want a good experience in Physics 3.

She's very nice and goes over content multiple times to make sure everyone understands the material. The weekly R assignments were annoying but a useful skill for anyone interested in coding. Practice exams are almost identical to the actual exams and if you make a decent effort to study those you are pretty much guaranteed an A. STAT100 is a pretty easy class but taking her made it even easier.

Assignments are almost free 100's, so it's down to the exams, which aren't too bad if you know your calculus (and can be bothered to study). He provides an extremely generous study guide with answers, and makes both his lecture recordings and writings accessible. No quizzes too, which is really nice. As generous as the assignments are I felt like Danul explained concepts in lecture in extremely roundabout and confusing ways, and I personally found it better to learn from the TA or the textbook as a primary source, but also useful to peek at the lecture notes and such secondarily.
Very clear at explaining statistics concepts, quizzes and exams are pretty easy. Only downsides are that his lectures can be quite dry and coding projects are somewhat annoying to do.

Not a good professor at all. Lectures were incredibly dull with him just reading verbatim off of the lecture slides, which were riddled with errors, including errors in formulas which I only noticed after slamming my head against a wall on a homework problem only to realize the formula HE GAVE was wrong, so maybe double-check the things he tells you to be safe. He paced the entire class incorrectly, as well, so we spent the entire first half of the semester doing the basic foundational work of STAT410, but we never made it to moments, characteristic functions, or limit theorems, all of which I would have liked to learn as a Math major interested in studying statistics. The exams were easy however and you can bring a formula sheet. Not particularly hard professor, but a genuinely awful teacher.

dr shapiro is very knowledgable and seems very confident on his expertise in ecology and evolution. however, i sometimes think he is TOO smart for the rest of us taking his class. his exams are by far the worst as he typically includes something that he briefly mentioned in lecture or asked us to recall something so specific from a video (which i think is ridiculous). if you dont go to class, youll likely miss something he said that will definitely be in the exam. he goes on too many tangents and can never just get to the point. he also talks about those stupid birds way too often. aside from the fact that he is a really bad lecturer, he also doesnt let us see our full grade for the whole semester so youre basically blindsided until he releases them. i strongly recommend taking any other professor than him if you actually want to get an A in a 100 level biology class.

Most of the bad ratings are for Mohan's lab, and the quality of your lab depends on your TA. But Mohan herself is a great lecturer. Really good professor, made the class pretty easy to understand and easy to find success. There is a lab manual that you have to buy (SimBio) and there are graded readings (but they're graded on completion), however you honestly don't need to read the textbook. Mohan only puts material that she goes over in lecture on the exams, and she records all of her lectures, and it was really convenient! Attendance matters however as she puts random participation questions in the lecture, so you will have to wake up at 9am and go to the lectures, but she drops like 7 of those participation question grades. Use frugally tho! A lot of the other reviews on here talk a lot about the other work she assigns throughout the semester, but it really isn't a lot and fairly easy. There are weekly in-class "quizzes" on Fridays which go over the material that she talked about throughout the week, so even if you do skip you should still keep up with the material. The exams are also fairly similar to the weekly class quizzes so they can help you get an idea of what kind of questions would be on the exam. You can also go to office hours, inbox the TAs, and go to Guided Study Sessions if you need help. GSS sessions are hosted two times a week at the same time. Overall this course with this professor was fairly easy imo, if you put a little bit of effort into the class you will succeed!

I never interacted with her, but her lab manual is a scam. You pay like $25 for a lab manual that is poorly written, confusing, and ridden with errors, and she has about 1000 or so students each semester all of which need to buy in order to succeed, so she is making bank scamming college students. She was super strict about small things. I turned in one assignment 3 minutes late, which is my fault, but I ended up getting 1/2 credit. Aside from her being super strict, your experience within the class will be reliant on your TA.

Absolute goat! Such a nice person and very knowledgeable about every subject within BSCI201. Her exams were fair, and you are given plenty of material to help you prepare and study for them. Her office hours were a big help too as almost no one goes for some reason. She also allows a cheat sheet for each exam that helps you avoid the stupid memory things that won't come up but just might be snuck in for a few questions on each exam. 10/10 professor I would 100% recommend.

Fletcher is a great professor. He records all his lectures and uploads them to Canvas, so really, the only time you have to attend class is when he hosts Group Activity assignments during class (GAEs). You will get full points on the homework and in-class GAEs for just attempting them. The online concept checks have three attempts and unlimited time, while the online GAE-preps have one attempt with unlimited time. He does ramble a bit during lectures but usually gets through everything he needs to just fine. You do get cheat sheets for all the exams, the front page of the equation sheet for all the midterms, and the front and back of the equation sheet for the final exam. I would have done better if I studied more, so just study a decent amount and write what you can't grasp onto the cheat sheet and you'll be fine. He also rounds up grades, my 86.45% was rounded up to an 87% for a B+.

There's a review that gave this man 5 stars and said the people who don't do well didn't study enough...NOT TRUE. He's a very smart man for sure but his lecture slides and speech are very disorganized and have no flow to it. Very hard to understand him and keep up with him in lecture, and his recordings aren't much better. His exams averaged low 70s and high 60s, which is just a reflection of his teaching because a majority of us would make Quizlets based off his lecture slides so we had all of the info, but he would still put questions that were so incredibly specific that you can't really know what the answer is unless you're a genius. He was also very disrespectful and condescending to students, would often tell them to "Shut up" or ask "Are you dumb" in lecture. I don't recommend if you want a good grade.

In the last four years I've taken two chems, two anatomies, two physics, and various other straining courses, and this by far is the worst. The content probably wouldn't be nearly as difficult to learn and understand if Dr. Tran used even half of the time we spend in lecture actually teaching us. She raves about how great the flipped classroom is, but if you were to ask literally anyone in our class you would not hear the same answer. We have to watch videos that are 3 years old and not a single minute of lecture is spent reiterating any material. Every class period is spent doing clicker questions for a participation grade, which the school no longer covers the subscription for, and we are expected to have the same level of understanding as her despite her not really teaching us. Most of class guesses on all of the questions and they are not a good indicator of exam questions. For every exam, Dr. Tran creates multiple versions where everyone had vastly different questions. To top it off, she informed TAs that they were not allowed to give us partial credit for most questions, even parts that were worth 10 points on a 150 point test. Every test had errors and had questions that were very poorly planned and worded. Truly the only reason I can expect to do well in this course is because of my TA Kari and what felt like hundreds of lab assignments. Most weeks we had 2 or 3 time consuming assignments due, in addition to 2 large projects that barely related to the class. We had to come up a gene and cloning strategy to genetically modify bacteria to benefit a cow???? This class has been one of the most time consuming courses ever, especially with two lab sessions a week. It is clear to me that Dr. Tran does not prioritize her students and doesn't really seem to care about how we are doing. She sent out a mid-semester survey for feedback and went over it in class. She proceeded to tell us that she won't be changing anything despite us asking for some change. I truly hated this class.

Dude is nice and is generally a good lecturer. Exams are EXTREMELY lecture-heavy and contains a lot of specific content that he TALKS about, but does not put in the slides. DO NOT take tues-thurs 75 minute lectures. This man does not stop talking the entire way through, and I guarantee you will fall asleep, zone out, or generally pray for the sweet release of the void. The mon-wed-fri lectures are less overwhelming.

Dr. Wu is a fantastic professor and if you are considering taking BSCI410 or an upper level biology course, then I would strongly recommend taking BSCI410 with her. I have found that it can be difficult to connect with professors at UMD who teach large courses with many students, and it can be easy to find yourself feeling like just another number associated with a grade on their roster, but it is completely different with Dr. Wu. She is a truly caring individual who wants her students to succeed and she is incredibly generous in terms of the time she commits to her students and her willingness to help students understand the course content and do well in her class. She is an incredibly nice and relatable person who is not intimidating at all which makes the course much more enjoyable, and she makes it very comfortable to reach out to her. Do not be intimidated by some of the reviews on here about her class, BSCI410 with her is incredibly fair and she makes it very possible to do well in her course. As an upper level biology course, BSCI410 has its fair share of challenging content, but if you reach out to Dr. Wu and attend office hours to sure up gaps in your knowledge related to the content then you will definitely do well. The course itself is also extremely interesting for anyone who has an interest in genetics or the life sciences. Some major topics covered in the class include genetic expression and interactions, genetic technologies, and genetic history. Dr. Wu makes these topics extremely enjoyable to learn about through providing fun examples related to the content during lecture and exercises outside of class time that are thought provoking and make you think about how what you are learning can be applied to the world around you. In terms of the graded course content, there are three exams, six homework assignments, twelve post-lecture elms quizzes, in class clicker questions and a handful of one minute essays online. She drops your lowest exam score, lowest homework score, two lowest quiz scores, and two lowest clicker scores, but if you attend office hours and talk to her about topics you are having trouble understanding then these dropped assignments serve more as assurance that you can relax going into the final than as a grade saver. When enrolling in my classes, I had the decision to take BSCI410 with Dr. Wu or another upper level biology course that looked easier but far less interesting and I am incredibly happy that I decided to take BSCI410. If you are reading this review and are on the fence about whether or not you should enroll in this course with Dr. Wu then I hope my review convinces you to go ahead and enroll as it has been one of my favorite classes I have taken at UMD and Dr. Wu is a fantastic professor and an amazing person.
I had her for chem over the summer and she was honestly great. I had an 89.something and that ended me with an A+. She took time to stay after class to answer questions and her tests were fair.

Lab is entirely TA-run. My TA was ok and ran the lab smoothly. You'll have some TAs who'll grade harshly and others who will be softer. Ultimately, your experience in this course depends on what TAs happen to grade your lab. The only reason why people took Guest this semester is because she was the ONLY option for this course. At least you will never interact with her in lab. This is why I'm giving her a one-star review: At the end of the semester, she unexpectedly curved everyone's grade DOWN by 3-5 percent (i.e. ~92 equates to a B+). I got a high 93% (raw percentage) which got dropped to an 88%. She states in her lab manual that "you should work as if there was no curve in this class"... so what does that mean if you curve down? This does not allow students to accurately keep track of their letter grades, and turns the class into a giant competition to get good grades. If you try to email her about that, you will be met with no response -- as other reviews have said, it is extremely difficult to communicate with her. For future students... do yourself a favor: if there is another option, go with that option. Although this isn't likely to change.

I thought Dr. Stocker was a really good teacher overall. She doesn't like to be emailed but is a very friendly person and helpful when I went to office hours. Some topics can be hard to understand but I always thought she explained them well, sometimes using fun metaphors. She doesn't post full lecture notes or recordings so you do always have to come to class. She does however post multiple practice exams, some with answer keys and some without and they tend to be pretty accurate. I do also think she makes you memorize some things like ion solubilities that other classes get charts on for exams.

Hey everyone, After reading some of the reviews here, I felt like I needed to share my experience. I took Organic Chemistry with Dr. H in the spring and ended up withdrawing. I thought I could “figure it out,” but that approach did not work for me. When I retook the course with Dr. H the following semester, everything changed. She genuinely believed in me and emphasized that success would come with consistent practice. I didn’t do anything over winter break to prepare, yet I ended up with an A- that semester. Honeslty, the difference was that I did orgo every single day. Dr. H’s exams are fair—they test whether you understand the concepts, not your ability to memorize random material. She never includes topics that haven’t been discussed in class. Chemistry is hard (I was in tears y'all), but blaming the exams isn’t fair—they are designed to reflect your understanding, and that’s exactly what she evaluates. I also went to office hours a few times for extra help, and she was incredibly supportive. Sure, sometimes I couldn’t grasp certain concepts right away, but she still guided me and pushed me to understand the material. Not every interaction will be great, but you get what you put into it. Honestly, I absolutely love Dr. H and would take CHEM 231 with her a million times over. Regardless of who you take you're going to have to work your butt off--that's just orgo for you. So, as long as you can explain why the heck you're drawing that arrow there you'll be fine :)

Never met her, you only interact with the TAs. The work for this class is actually insane considering it’s only 1 credit. You have to do the pre lab write up and pre lab worksheet for the current weeks lab but then another post lab worksheet and post lab questions for the previous weeks lab. Pre-labs arent that much work and sometimes the pre lab/post lab worksheets arent bad either, but the post lab questions are so long and tedious. The TAs lowkey grade harsh too. Go to the TAs office hours for help on the PLQs and sometimes the post lab worksheets too. Find a TA who will give you the answers bc some are stuck up and wont help you unless you attempt it first. If youre wondering abt the curve I got a 78% rounded to a B.

She gives off the vibe that she doesn’t really want to be teaching, and she kept mentioning that she wanted a promotion throughout the semester. The class itself is full of people who are the teacher's pets and act like everything she says is hilarious, which is honestly kind of exhausting. She flies through lectures at lightning speed and I seriously couldn’t retain anything in real time, so I had to start recording every class just to have a chance of understanding it later. That said, when I did go back and review the recordings, the material actually made more sense. So I’ll give her credit, she does prepare you well if you're willing to put in the extra effort to basically relearn everything yourself. Her exams are fair, and she provides tons of practice problems and old tests to study from. But she doesn’t record lectures or post notes herself, which feels outdated and unfair given how fast she goes. Overall, she clearly knows the material and can prepare students well, but the delivery makes it really hard to keep up unless you're HYPER motivated or already strong in orgo.

Literally do anything you can not to take this class. these reviews don't even do how bad she is at teaching justice. It is awful. I went to class the first two weeks - all she did was make me more confused. First, she would spend 10 minutes figuring how to work the technology. Then she would spend half the class figuring how to do her own problems. Im not sure about y'all but if a teacher cant figure it out neither can i. It was way easier to self study and just go to discussion rather than try to sit through those classes. On top of this, the homework she gives is so god AWFUL. I would spend literally 10 hours a week on JUST the homework - because if you get one question wrong it will take you back one (so as if you didn't get the previous question right) which is genuinely the most frustrating thing in the world. Mind you this is a two credit class, so spending upwards of 10 hours on homework a week is INSANEEEEE. take anyone else. please its for your own health and wellbeing. what i will say constructively about this class: since i didnt go to class, the homework did help keep me familiarized with the topics so i wasnt so screwed when it came time for exams - but like 100% that does not outweigh the trauma that ALEKS (homework website) put me through. also, her exams are not super unfair, they are kinda ish similar to the practice exams she gives butttttttttt she will throw in one or two or three like SUPER hard questions on every exam that absolutely nobody gets right just for fun (TA literally said that she just does this and thats what differentiates the A students from everyone else).

Dr. Brooks is an unusual character. Some days she seems so nice and is willing to help you out any way possible, and some days it seems like she has pms and hates the world and wants you to get an F. All I can say is that I worked by @$$ off to get an A in this class, and it was the most workload I had out of any class. She curved the class so that if you had an 85% or higher, you would get an A. The three exams were difficult, especially the multiple choice part. Although the final was really easy, just make sure you write all the procedures and every chart from the lab manual. Overall if you really want to get A, get ready to work.
if you have him, you are in big trouble. Every one-star review you see here it's even worse than that!! and if you have no coding background imma just say you gonna go in som deep stress for sure.

Insanely boring professor with the strictest rules. No missing class whatsoever, unless you have a university approved reason, and even if you submit an absence request he won't respond for weeks on end until finally denying you weeks after the request was made. No electronics in class, including ipads. Not a problem, just buy a notebook, but just seems so unnecessary. Reminds you to call him Larry in every lecture and gets weirdly upset if someone refers to him as a professor. Only bright part is that he occasionally makes jokes about frogs and other animals but the fact that he docks points from your grade for the craziest things- accidentally writing down the wrong discussion time on a midterm, forgetting to write your name on the odd numbered pages- takes away from any sort of friendly jokes he might make.

If you are reading this in order to decide what professor to take and you are early enough to not pick Yoon, don't. However, do not stress for the months leading up to the course if you have to take him like I did. His course is not equivalent to all of these reviews and you should go in with a more positive mindset than these reviews let on. I am not a genius, in fact I was just hoping to pass 216 knowing how hard it would be, especially with Yoon. Without a doubt, my friends in Nelson and Kauffman had a much easier time and arguably learned more. However, Yoon does not mean you are failing the class, I ended with a B. What it takes to do well in this class is hard work. His exams are impossible and not fair. They do not resemble the material taught in class, so doing bad on the exams I would say is expected (class average was no higher than a 66). The projects are totally doable, start early. The lab assignments are also free As if you attend labs. I did not miss a single lecture or lab. I tried very hard on projects and lab assignments trying to get as many "free" points as I could which will balance out the exam grades. What it comes down to as well is that Yoon is truly such a nice guy. I had an emergency and he granted me an extension without even considering it. You have to take advantage of his willingness to help. I went to Yoon's personal office hours multiple times to ask questions from lectures or go over exam questions. During these sessions I learned a ton. You should try very hard to build a relationship with Yoon and start this early in the semester. While the class was averaging low scores, he gave us an easy extra credit assignment towards the end of the semester and yes at the end of the course, he did curve our final grades. In conclusion, I wouldnt be eager to take his classes and he makes it very difficult but trying to get as many points as you can and studying enough to stay with the average on exams will get you very far. Most importantly, review the lecture slides after class and if you are confused GO SEE HIM!!!

Easy class imo. Easy exams, pretty straightforward. You have to go to discussion on wednesdays because there are quizzes that are about class topic the week before. His lectures are recorded and it is not mandatory to go to class and they are some what boring but really helpful. Homeworks are long and can be tricky but start early and spend time on them and understand it, they will help alot with exams. Highly recommend taking 250 with him!

Conflates incompetence with "challenging students." Agree with his philosophy of not revealing exam answers, but when all students get are typo-ridden exams and brief, disorganized overview lectures on exam topics, it's egregiously obvious how little effort Max puts into writing assignments and exams. The responsibility of knowing course material falling solely on the student as detailed on the syllabus is unreasonable given that undergraduate students have not committed to becoming data science specialists, and near contemptible given Max's example.

CS 330, a hard class they say, But I never did much work anyways They groan and they sweat and sometimes they cry But to that I say "I didn't even have to try" Speaking seriously, Cliff's 330 is a great class and not very difficult. You'll learn a lot from his projects. Take him!

Best TA UMD CS will have for a long time. She sacrificed a lot for us. Staying up to record problem guides for students. Staying past OH hours to help students. Very proactive on piazza. Blessed to have had her as a TA while taking this notoriously difficult course.
Micheal doesn't teach you and expects you to learn all of the material outside of the class.

His lectures are mediocre, but the real problem is how he tests code. He puts our arbitrary project specs without public/release tests and then tests them in a very specific way, causing many students to get zeros for things such as putting a space in the wrong place in the output. He said he would fix this, but I still have no idea what grade I have in this class.

Marsh's greatest contribution to the field of college education is getting out of the way of his students by letting them do the course self-paced. That comes with its own risks that you do in fact fall behind. But do not expect any help from him or the TAs through your journey, you're on your own.

Regli started out seeming like an accomplished and interesting professor, but as the semester went on that facade faded. He is one of the most disrespectful professors I have ever had. The first programming assignment he gave us had 3 conflicting sets of instructions, took the longest of any cs project I've ever taken (for some people ~40+ hours), and was detrimentally open ended, which is something I normally appreciate. His exam questions are extremely vague and have no clear answer. You can know your stuff and still fail the exam because you have no idea what the questions are asking. Overall this has been the least organized and most condescending class I have ever taken. Regli sees himself as above the students and above the class. He has not dealt with the material in 30 year and when pressed on an answer will just try to make you look stupid. Take this class if you have to, it won't be the end of the world, but you will probably hate him and the class.

The only pros to this semester were that the dreaded B+ tree, the E/R Project, and the math-related projects are removed. Spark is a separate project and MongoDB was another separate project, along with a new JDBC/ODBC project. That's the only reason why I'm giving this review two stars, since the projects were actually useful and were a lot easier than they were in the past, and from the generous late policy. But other than that, this was miserable. Each topic no matter how complex it is was gone through in such surface level so then we have to pick up extra time ourselves to thoroughly learn the concepts, especially canonical cover, and concurrency. For canonical cover, we were just supposed to look up an algorithm instead which was ridiculous. Also, the fact that we have to study I don't know a 1000 slides for an exam that can ask about literally anything is ridiculous too. I could be fine with all of this if the homeworks had detailed solutions after them. Some answers are just marked as "Correct" or "Incorrect" without giving us the full answer, and how we get to that answer. Also, as I mentioned earlier in learning the material on our own, examples were not given well at all. Examples should mimic homework difficulty so then we can learn from them and apply to the homework problems, not learning them in surface level and then having to take a lot of extra time just to do the complex ones. And with the late policy, official solutions can't be released, which I understand that. But if that's the case, then we need more complex examples with solutions so we have a point of reference. Overall, this class was just a lot. If you want to learn databases, you're better off learning it on your own.

Lectures are great for learning concepts, clearly has a ton of knowledge and is passionate and kind. For the projects most of the learning has come from TA led overviews/course notes for projects also written by TAs. Projects done in groups of 3-4 and are challenging but I personally feel they are rewarding. Midterm was fairly tough but according to the TAs it will be curved fairly well. Would recommend for anyone with a passion for learning or interest in these topics, would recommend starting projects early with your group.

Definitely the best professor for CMSC451. The lecture videos are concise, well put together, and very informative. The course was also structured in a way that allowed for a lot of flexibility for students. Exams are fair and you will do well if you do the homework's. Professor Childs is very knowledgeable about algorithms and is also able to answer questions and explain concepts very well. Overall, really enjoyed his class.

Dr. Washington was great and the nicest professor. He was interesting everyday and had his material ready. Unfortunately, he had generally low standards for how much material to cover in the class, and if you really want to take cryptology to know the material at an advanced level, don't take it with him. If you want to take it for fun and to learn a few things about cryptology, take it with him, because you will learn!

Aric is the absolute man. He is so understanding and willing to compromise if you need an extension. This is also the class in which I've learned the most in my entire experience. I came in as a very below average coder but Aric got me up to speed and now I'm so much more comfortable with Python. The workload is definitely not easy but he's a fantastic teacher. Also a great lecturer. My favorite professor thus far for sure.

This class is so easy. Only reason I got a B is because I slacked off during an exam and didn’t do the study guide. Every other exam I aced. As long as you attend lectures and do the study guides you’ll be fine. The study guides are the exact same as the midterms just different numbers so you’re ready for them. He’s also got some pretty solid jokes. Only tough part is that he doesn’t make the final. But he does his best to make sure you’re prepared. Absolutely loved his class!

Having Foivos as your TA will be the best decision you make if taking MATH141! Calc 2 is difficult, but he makes it manageable and breaks down difficult concepts so that you actually understand what you’re learning. Math is not my strong suit, and this was the first math class that actually made sense, and it was due to his teaching style. He genuinely cares about his students and always makes time to help students when they are stuck or struggling. Even with the head injury I received while taking his course, he was able to accommodate and teach, which I feel says a lot about his character! Don’t second guess it—if you have a pulse, take Foivos!

Archana is a very kind professor and takes a genuine interest in ensuring that students who put in effort get a good grade. She holds review sessions for the three midterms and multiple for the final regardless of how many show up. These helped me in understanding concepts the most out of all resources. Quizzes are during discussion and you can take them in collaboration (two get dropped). If you understand what is going on in the quizzes you most likely are up to speed with the class. Overall, she is lenient, genuine, and nice, and if you are ever struggling in the course go to her office hours and she will help you without hesitation as long as you are genuine. Just make sure to stay attentive in lecture or you may find yourself lost after a few lectures.

Here's the entire class (no quizzes): - 2 Midterm Exams each worth 100 points. - 1 Final worth 200 points - 3 matlab homeworks that are 10 points each, all doable in like at most 2 hours (you literally just copy code from the guide sheet) Otherwise, lectures are useless because he's very theory heavy and just uses notes from another teacher, but also throws in physics concepts randomly for no reason? He'll spend entire classes doing this btw. Exams are average difficulty, but he gives like 0 prep, just tells you to do certain recommended problems in the textbook. The funny part is that even if you do go to lecture, stuff on the final STILL will show up that he just never covers (trust me, problems on the final will be nothing like anything he gives). Take Grillakis if you just want to teach yourself and take mid-difficulty exams. Don't bother EVER going to lecture. If you're stuck taking him just watch Justin's videos and use his notes (look up justin wyss gallifent, he has a website and youtube channel) and pray that the final is easy.

I highly recommend this professor for Differential Equations. She possesses a deep understanding of the subject and delivers material with confidence, all while being incredibly kind and approachable with her students. She successfully balances the course's inherent rigor with a commitment to student comprehension, taking every necessary step to ensure everyone understands the content. I truly hope to see her teach more courses in the Math Department in the future.

I'm only getting a C because I bombed my first midterm. The homework feels like a lot of work because it's due right when you finish learning the material that is covered in the homework and you're not able to solve it easily just yet. But I promise when you look back at the homework questions to study for the final, you'll realize how easy it is to solve them and laugh at yourself for spending so much time than necessary. It took me a lot of self-studying to fully understand how to write proofs, but once you understand everything the material becomes fun. Dr Truman is a great professor, she'll do anything to help you understand the material, so don't worry too much !

**Note: I took this as a summer course.** Allan is extremely adept at explaining math concepts beyond theory. He is helpful, understanding, and genuinely wants students to succeed. I found this course to be much easier than 461 because I learn best through real-life examples... and this class is all about real-life examples. We used free online textbooks, but I found that the lectures were enough. We covered a different (yet related) subject every 2 days with group work due at the end of the second lecture. The group work is done during lecture time and is basically a work sheet that you can talk through with a couple other students in a breakout room. Similar to his 461 class, MATLAB was a major part of the homework. I'd highly recommend making a class GroupMe and meeting separately on zoom because some of the homeworks can be long and difficult. Exams were fair; it was open note, open book, and had similar questions to previous exams (he provided previous exam solutions). However, a lot of people felt rushed to finish the exams on time. The average exam score was 79%, with the median being 82%. Pros: - Recorded lectures - Groupwork is probably a completion grade... don't quote me on that - Useful feedback/explanations provided on homework submissions - Open note, open book exams Cons: - Some homework problems take hours to figure out - May not have enough time on exams - Lectures aren't directly engaging or personable, only 1 other person had their camera on

Abstract Algebra was probably the most difficult course I have taken so far in college, but it was all worth it because I learned an incredible amount thanks to Justin's awesome teaching skills! I had him for 246 last semester, so I decided to give this class a try because he was teaching it. 403 was a very tough course for me, but I'm sure I would have failed the class if any other professor had taught it. Justin lectures is such a straightforward, easy-to-follow manner and explains everything he writes of the chalkboard. He provides plenty of examples so that everyone can comprehend the meaning of theorems, definitions, and proofs he writes on the board. Unlike most of the professors in the math department, Justin actually cares about his students and doesn't brush them off.
